facts.text: MongoDB Atlas on AWS supports two private networking models: VPC Peering (legacy) and AWS PrivateLink (recommended). Both complement the Network Access List (IP allowlist) for controlling cluster access.
The private endpoint-aware connection string has a different hostname:
Not the standard mongodb+srv://cluster0.abcde.mongodb.net.
Security Groups as access list entries: For applications running in EC2/ECS/Lambda within a VPC, using Security Group IDs as access list entries is more dynamic and avoids managing CIDR ranges.
Atlas uses SRV DNS records (_mongodb._tcp.<hostname>) for cluster discovery. When connecting over PrivateLink, verify:
DNS resolves to private IPs (not public Atlas IPs)
Security groups allow TCP on ports returned by SRV records (typically 1024-65535 for PrivateLink)
For centralized networking with many VPCs:
Create Atlas PrivateLink endpoint in a "hub" VPC
Connect hub VPC to AWS Transit Gateway
All application VPCs access Atlas via Transit Gateway → hub → PrivateLink
Route table: 10.0.0.0/8 → Transit Gateway in spoke VPCs
Transit Gateway also enables cross-account Atlas access without creating separate PrivateLink endpoints per account.
Atlas uses IAM role assumption (not IAM user credentials) to access the KMS key. Configure via Atlas Cloud Provider Access (Unified AWS Access) → creates a cross-account IAM role.
Failsafe: If KMS is inaccessible, running mongod continues (DEK cached in memory) but will not restart.
Route Atlas alert events to EventBridge:
Atlas UI → Integrations → AWS EventBridge → provide AWS account ID
Atlas creates an EventBridge partner event source
Create EventBridge rule to route events to Lambda, SQS, SNS, etc.
MongoDB is an AWS ISV Accelerate partner:
Co-sell eligibility: MongoDB opportunities can qualify for AWS funding
AWS Marketplace listing for Atlas (PAYG and committed-use)
AWS Marketplace purchases appear on AWS invoice
ISV Workload Migration Program: potential AWS credits for customer migration projects
Connection timeout after PrivateLink setup:
Verify using the PrivateLink connection string (not standard)
Check security group allows outbound TCP 27017 (or 1024-65535 for SRV)
Verify private_dns_enabled = false on the AWS endpoint
Confirm Atlas private endpoint status = AVAILABLE
DNS resolving to public IP:
Route53 private hosted zone may be interfering
Verify no conflicting private hosted zone for mongodb.net
From EC2 in VPC: nslookup <private-endpoint-hostname> should return private IP
VPC Peering connection not routing:
Route table in application VPC must include route to Atlas VPC CIDR
Route table in Atlas VPC (managed by MongoDB) is auto-updated
CIDR overlap check: Atlas VPC uses 192.168.x.x - ensure no overlap with your VPC
